key_insight: LLM systems enriched with clinical knowledge can identify in-hospital cardiac arrest from EHR notes more accurately than ICD-code algorithms.
clinical_relevance: These models could reduce manual chart review by prioritizing likely IHCA encounters for clinician adjudication and registry surveillance.
method: Guideline-enriched prompting to inject physician-defined clinical knowledge
Supervised fine-tuning on EHR note data for IHCA detection and location extraction
Self-correction step in a two-pass workflow to improve decision quality
evidence_signal: On a curated evaluation corpus, the fine-tuned LLM achieved precision 0.88, recall 1.00, and F1 0.94, outperforming an ICD-based approach (precision 0.68, recall 0.91, F1 0.78).
watch_item: Performance dropped on a larger real-world validation cohort when the fine-tuned model could not self-correct, so deployment may need a separate correction stage and external validation.
paper_title: Beyond ICD Codes: Fine-Tuning LLMs for In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Identification from EHR Notes
